title: Cross-SDK explainable backoff profiles, deterministic id-key semantics, and retryable-error taxonomy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Define and ship a cross-language set of default retry/backoff profiles that are easy to reason about, plus deterministic idempotency key semantics and a compact retryable-error taxonomy for our Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Deliverables: spec doc, example snippets per language, SDK changes (flags/config), test harness and a small migration guide for customers.
motivation: Customers frequently ask what the SDK will do when transient errors occur during streaming or generation. We need defaults that balance latency and cost while avoiding surprising duplicate side-effects. A clear taxonomy helps SDKs and server-side policies make consistent retry decisions and gives users predictable semantics for idempotent and non-idempotent operations.
acceptance_criteria: Unified spec reviewed and approved by SDK leads (Python/TS/Go)
Three canonical backoff profiles implemented in each SDK: conservative, balanced, aggressive
Idempotency key semantics documented and enforced via SDK helper APIs with examples
Retryable-error taxonomy created and published; server-side and SDK mappings are aligned
End-to-end test harness simulating transient server errors for streaming and request-level retries
Migration guidance and changelog entry present for breaking behavioral changes
tasks: Draft spec: explainable backoff profiles + how to pick one
Define deterministic id-key rules: key generation, rotation, TTL, and scope
Create retryable-error taxonomy with canonical categories and example HTTP/grpc codes
Implement SDK flags/config: redwood.retry.profile and redwood.retry.id_key_hint
Add examples to SDK docs for Python/TS/Go demonstrating best practices
Build integration tests with simulated transient errors and streaming interruptions
Run an internal canary to validate no customer-impacting duplicate side-effects
decisions: Expose three named profiles rather than many micro-tunable knobs to improve discoverability
Use the server-provided idempotency-hint header when present; otherwise SDK generates a collated deterministic key by default
Streaming resume will be idempotent by sequence token whenever supported; otherwise clients fall back to request-level retry with conservative profile
Treat 429, TCP connection resets, and gRPC UNAVAILABLE as retryable transient errors; treat 4xx client errors as non-retryable unless explicitly whitelisted
tradeoffs_and_risks: Aggressive profile reduces tail latency but increases duplicate-side-effect risk for non-idempotent endpoints
Automatic id-key generation reduces friction but could accidentally correlate retries across logical operations if customers misuse high-level batching APIs
A narrow taxonomy reduces cognitive load but may hide edge cases that require custom handling by advanced customers

review_feedback: PM (Lina Morales): favor conservative default for hosted API to avoid accidental customer-side effects
Security (Omar Singh): ensure id-key values are never logged by default and integrate with KMS for sensitive operations
Platform (Eva Müller): request that SDK respect server-side Retry-After headers and rate-limit directives
Docs (Maya Chen): add cookbook examples showing how to opt into aggressive profile for latency-sensitive non-mutating reads
implementation_notes: SDKs will add a small shim layer that normalizes the profile selection and id-key generation. The server will accept id-key in header 'X-Redwood-Id-Key' and expose 'Retry-After' semantics. For streaming, SDKs will prefer in-stream resume tokens; where unavailable, the client will fall back to per-request retry behavior following the chosen profile.
examples: Python: from redwood.sdk import RetryProfile, id_key_from_context  # use RetryProfile.BALANCED for default
Go: opts := redwood.RetryOptions{Profile: redwood.RetryBalanced, IdKeyHint: fmt.Sprintf("user-%d", uid)}
migration_notes: Change is backward-compatible if customers leave profile unset (defaults to BALANCED). Customers relying on previous undocumented retry semantics should test against staging. Provide a CLI tool to scan application logs for potential duplicate side-effect patterns before enabling aggressive profile.
